intro: Sales managers negotiate, persuade and lead teams, skills that every senior business role needs. The closest of the 25 careers below is Purchasing Managers, with an 89% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $148,080, about the same as the $148,270 sales managers earn.
why_it_works: Leading a sales team means setting targets, coaching people through rejection and closing big deals yourself. O*NET rates negotiation at 4 out of 5 for sales managers, and persuasion, social perceptiveness and managing people at 3.88. Purchasing, HR and finance leadership use the same people skills. Because pay is already high, only 5 matches pay more. The gaps are managing money and materials.
tips: Purchasing is the quietest switch: same pay, and you negotiate from the buyer's side.
Computer and Information Systems Managers earn $175,140, which is 18% more, if you sell technology now.
Take on budget ownership in your current role; financial management is a common gap.

faq.q: What jobs can former sales managers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Purchasing Managers (89%), Financial Managers (83%) and Chief Executives (83%), based on O*NET 31.0. Human Resources Managers are also 83% matched and earn $149,280, which is 1% more than the $148,270 sales manager median.

faq.q: Which careers for sales managers pay more?
faq.a: 5 of the 25 matches pay more. Chief Executives earn $213,990 (44% more), Computer and Information Systems Managers $175,140 (18% more) and Financial Managers $166,570 (12% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Executive roles usually need a graduate degree or long experience.

faq.q: Do sales managers need another degree?
faq.a: Usually not. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than sales managers already have, and 3 usually need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 53% of workers in the closest match, so your sales record and team results matter most.

faq.q: What skills should sales managers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are troubleshooting, managing financial resources, technology design and managing materials. Persuasion already rates 3.88 out of 5 for sales managers in O*NET, so budgets and operations, not selling, are the main gaps.
